questions.question:
11 is related to 121 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 22 is related to 484. To which of the following is 31

related, following the same logic?

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent

digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1

and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number)² = 2nd number.

Now,

For, 11 : 121

⇒ 11² = 121.

For, 22 : 484

⇒ 22² = 484.

Similarly, for 31 ∶ ?

**⇒ 31² = 961.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some vegetables are fruits.

Some fruits are flowers.

All flowers are garlands.

Conclusions:

I. Some garlands are fruits.

II. Some vegetables are flowers.

III. Some vegetables are garlands.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dd4438caf462caddc83defd971d4438ec0f3721c3f194c3aa84892d820a4e301.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some garlands are fruits → Follow (As some fruits are flowers and all flowers are garlands. As some part of fruits is common with flowers which whole comes in garlands, therefore it is true.)

II. Some vegetables are flowers → **Does not **follow (As some vegetables are fruits and some fruits are flowers. So it is possible but not definite.)

III. Some vegetables are garlands → Does not follow (As some vegetables are fruits, some fruits are flowers and all flowers are garlands. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion I follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question:
The same operation(s) are followed in all the given number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent

digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1

and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Option 1) 7 : 15

__(7 × 2)__ + 1 = 15

__14 + 1__ = 15

15 = 15 (LHS = RHS)

Option 2) 11 : 121

__(11 × 2)__ + 1 = 121

__22 + 1__ = 121

23 ≠ 121 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 3) 22 : 45

__(22 × 2)__ + 1 = 45

__44 + 1__ = 45

45 = 45 (LHS = RHS)

Option 4) 5 : 11

__(5 × 2)__ + 1 = 11

__10 + 1__ = 11

11 = 11 (LHS = RHS)

Thus, out of all the options '11 : 121' is the odd one out.

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(24, 15, 120)

(21, 19, 133)

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent

digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1

and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number × 2nd number) ÷ 3 = 3rd number.

Now,

For, 24, 15, 120

⇒ (24 × 15) ÷ 3

⇒ 360 ÷ 3 = 120.

For, (21, 19, 133)

⇒ (21 × 19) ÷ 3

⇒ 399 ÷ 3 = 133

Similarly, for** (27, 12, 108)**

**⇒ (27 × 12) ÷ 3**

**⇒ 324 ÷ 3 = 108.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.
